import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/training_3.csv"

Source3_38_0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
Source3_38_1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
Source3_38_2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
Source3_38_3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_38_0 and Source3_38_2 on "batsman"
join_0_2 = pd.merge(Source3_38_0, Source3_38_2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Operation 2: JOIN Source3_38_1 and Source3_38_3 on "batsman"
join_1_3 = pd.merge(Source3_38_1, Source3_38_3, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Operation 3: JOIN the results of previous joins (join_0_2 and join_1_3) on "batsman"
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_2, join_1_3, on="batsman", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Operation 4: GROUP BY Source3_38_0.batsman (which is now join_all.batsman)
# Aggregations:
# avg(Source3_38_3.batsman_runs)  -> avg of join_1_3.batsman_runs (which is join_all.batsman_runs_y)
# sum(Source3_38_0.total_runs)    -> sum of join_0_2.total_runs (join_all.total_runs_x)
# avg(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> avg of join_0_2.batsman_runs (join_all.batsman_runs_x)
# sum(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> sum of join_0_2.batsman_runs (join_all.batsman_runs_x)

# Note: join_all columns:
# batsman
# total_runs_x (from Source3_38_0)
# batsman_runs_x (from Source3_38_2)
# total_runs_y (from Source3_38_1)
# batsman_runs_y (from Source3_38_3)

# We only need aggregations on:
# avg(Source3_38_3.batsman_runs) -> avg of batsman_runs_y
# sum(Source3_38_0.total_runs) -> sum of total_runs_x
# avg(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> avg of batsman_runs_x
# sum(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> sum of batsman_runs_x

agg_df = join_all.groupby("batsman").agg(
    batsman_runs_x_avg = ("batsman_runs_x", "mean"),
    total_runs_sum = ("total_runs_x", "sum"),
    batsman_runs_x_avg_dup = ("batsman_runs_x", "mean"),  # duplicate avg for clarity, will drop later
    batsman_runs_x_sum = ("batsman_runs_x", "sum"),
    batsman_runs_y_avg = ("batsman_runs_y", "mean"),
).reset_index()

# The target schema is:
# ['batsman': string, 'batsman_runs_x': float, 'total_runs': integer, 'batsman_runs_y': float, 'batsman_runs': integer]

# From the aggregations:
# batsman_runs_x: avg(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> use batsman_runs_x_avg
# total_runs: sum(Source3_38_0.total_runs) -> total_runs_sum (convert to int)
# batsman_runs_y: avg(Source3_38_3.batsman_runs) -> batsman_runs_y_avg
# batsman_runs: sum(Source3_38_2.batsman_runs) -> batsman_runs_x_sum (convert to int)

# Drop the duplicate avg column batsman_runs_x_avg_dup
agg_df = agg_df.drop(columns=["batsman_runs_x_avg_dup"])

# Rename columns to match target schema
agg_df = agg_df.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs_x_avg": "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs_sum": "total_runs",
    "batsman_runs_y_avg": "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_x_sum": "batsman_runs"
})

# Convert total_runs and batsman_runs to integer as per target schema
agg_df["total_runs"] = agg_df["total_runs"].round().astype(int)
agg_df["batsman_runs"] = agg_df["batsman_runs"].round().astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema order
agg_df = agg_df[["batsman", "batsman_runs_x", "total_runs", "batsman_runs_y", "batsman_runs"]]

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_38/target_multisource.csv"
agg_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
